d122df1faa64.justification: Pointer selects over runtime address literals materialize address bytes into the dst slot, so alloc must size the dst like any 2-byte value; folded pointer selects stay virtual.

379477b79d9c.justification: PAGE() is a pseudo-function gpasm does not know; each occurrence must resolve to its literal page bits.

8bc1ce1a3b8d.justification: Hand-derived expected values from the driver e2e for the irq=4 PIR2 arm, so the sim assertions are readable.

9368df7b9529.justification: Fixture header: the three pinned clang shapes, the sim preload contract, and the hand-computed expectations per irq value.

ba387e532d5d.justification: e2e doc: the three shapes under test, the SFR addresses, and the hand-derived flag sums per irq value.

2bab5595606f.justification: Hand-trace of the irq=0 run: INTCON preload, GetFlag sum, ClearFlag effect, direct PIR1 write.

bc1c33f02cf7.justification: parse_ty accepts the ptr token the canonical text emits, mirroring irparse's ty_of mapping to I16.

e317206bae1c.justification: Round-trip test for the new inttoptr instruction, pinning its parse/serialize and I16 widths.

40c986a49bee.justification: irparse captures the ptr phi token the same way the ir crate parser does.

76eb1c647087.justification: irparse splits inttoptr from the cast bundle so its dst is a pointer VALUE, distinct from a zext value.

66cb7541b4c7.justification: The IntToPtr dst slot holds the two address bytes; materialization is a plain 2-byte copy, and iselcore seeds it indirect.

cfbaa67a874a.justification: A folded pointer select emits nothing on PIC18; only the const-arm shape materializes.

ff8e6fdf8c82.justification: Two base kinds hold runtime address bytes for pointer-value materialization; both read as base+k+terms. Literal bases stay loud panics.

9092881410c9.justification: PIC18 const-arm select unit test: chosen address bytes land in the slot, deref through FSR0/INDF0.

c0277c34b470.justification: PIC14 emit_load_byte: runtime slots (ptr param and IntToPtr dst) both hold address bytes readable as the pointer value.

12ad1c85938a.justification: IntToPtr on PIC14 is an equal-width copy of the address bytes into the seeded indirect slot.

13a2abe60774.justification: Const-arm ptr select on PIC14 materializes the chosen arm's two address bytes as a value select.

502383eaeb0c.justification: Folded pointer selects emit nothing; the runtime-address literal select is the one that materializes.

143f5d6500f5.justification: PIC14 shape-1 unit test: standalone inttoptr derefs through FSR/INDF with no BANKSEL.

a07dd5442b2d.justification: The IntToPtr copy writes the address bytes into the slot before FSR setup reads them.

176027ea6336.justification: PIC14 select unit test: both literal arms materialize and the deref goes indirect with no BANKSEL.

b6e5db80338f.justification: PIC14 phi unit test: the GetFlag -O1 join shape, phi copies move address bytes then indirect deref.

5e4e80703997.justification: iselcore seeds every IntToPtr dst as an indirect slot: its bytes are the runtime address.

0d453de9a654.justification: iselcore seeds const-arm pointer selects as indirect slots: the select writes the chosen address bytes.

3ed3b9953f86.justification: iselcore seeds pointer phis whose incoming are all runtime addresses; a folded arm cannot be an incoming.

67a0b6614f20.justification: Only ptr-typed phis are pointer values; a value phi must never seed an indirect slot.

0d15450fcfe7.justification: A qualifying phi incoming reg is one already seeded as a runtime slot with no fold offset.

d8a22e5e074d.justification: const-arm selects were seeded as slots; the fold pass skips them since their bytes come from the select materialization.
